eyebrow: Python for Data Science · Chapter 4, Lesson 19
subtitle: Long format for machines, wide format for humans — moving between the two.

eyebrow: Setup — merge and a month column
caption: Long format: one row per observation — one city, one month, one amount.

code:
m.pivot_table(index="city", columns="status",
              values="amount", aggfunc="sum")
# Austin: returned 45.0, shipped 630.49
# Denver, pending: 0.0 (not NaN — amount is missing, sum treats it as 0)
caption: Like an Excel PivotTable in code — cities down the side, statuses across the top, sums in the cells.

eyebrow: margins, fill_value, and a sanity check
code:
m.pivot_table(index="city", columns="month",
              values="amount", aggfunc="sum", margins=True)
# bottom row: 255.49, 385.25, 259.99 — matches resample() from Lesson 16
caption: fill_value=0 replaces NaN cells; margins=True adds an All row/column — a good cross-check against other totals.

code:
pd.crosstab(m["city"], m["status"])
# Austin: 1 returned, 3 shipped
# Boston: 1 cancelled, 2 shipped
caption: Shorter than pivot_table when all you want is counts of combinations.

code:
monthly = m.groupby(["city", "month"], as_index=False)["amount"].sum()
wide = monthly.pivot(index="city", columns="month", values="amount")

m.pivot(index="city", columns="status", values="amount")
# ValueError: duplicate entries, cannot reshape
caption: pivot needs each index/column combination to appear once — pivot_table resolves duplicates; pivot can't.

eyebrow: melt: from wide back to long
caption: id_vars stays put; every other column stacks into two new ones — quarter and sales.
